_what: The Community Library, L-Space and Oook: every quotation on those three pages, the collections on the library's front desk, and the threads at the end of L-space. Built into the pages, and into the liner notes, by tools/make-library.py. The prose round them is hand-written in the pages and is ours; everything here is either somebody else's words, with their name, their work and their year, or a link to one of our own pages on stimpunks.org.
_source: Every quotation here was read off our own Library page, https://stimpunks.org/library/ (modified 2026-07-24), in the Knowledge System mirror, and copied word for word from that page on 2026-09-25. NONE OF THEM WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE BOOK OR THE RECORDING IT COMES FROM, and each entry says so in `checked` rather than looking like it had been, because an unchecked quotation must not sit among checked ones looking identical. Where our page gives no source at all, the entry says that too. The book links were resolved against Open Library's search on 2026-09-25 rather than copied, and one of them is why (see `_graphic_novel`).
_graphic_novel: OUR LIBRARY PAGE LINKS THE WRONG GUARDS! GUARDS! Its citation for the Librarian passage reads 'Guards! Guards!: A Discworld Novel (pp. 3-4). HarperCollins' and links Open Library work OL21372059W, edition OL7878556M. Asked on 2026-09-25, that edition answers as Gollancz, 2000, 122 pages, ISBN 0575070714, and the work lists Stephen Briggs and Graham Higgins beside Pratchett: it is the graphic-novel adaptation, not the 1989 novel the quotation is out of. The novel is OL453735W, first published 1989. make-library.py refuses both of the adaptation's ids, because the friendly edit is to copy the link off our own page, which looks sourced. The page on stimpunks.org is that site's to correct.

_cap.why: These rooms quote a handful of named lines the prose round them is about, which is Covenstead's case rather than the Zibaldone's, so the cap is set here rather than borrowed. Forty fits the longest line these rooms need, Pratchett's ball of string, and refuses the long passages our Library page quotes whole: the Librarian's arrival in Guards! Guards! runs to well over a hundred words and stays on that page, linked, where it is already cited. Raise this on purpose, with the reason written down, and never to fit one passage.

_refused: Two things on our Library page are deliberately not in these rooms. THE LINDA LINDAS' LINE is a lyric, and a lyric is refused on this street in every room but one, which holds a written permission (see DECISIONS.md and make-small-hours.py); the library says that libraries and punk share the same bones and leaves the song on the band's own record. THE PHOTOGRAPHS AND THE PAINTING are there under CC BY-NC-ND 2.0, CC BY-NC-SA 2.0 and a painter's own copyright, none of which this site's CC BY-SA 4.0 can carry, so they stay on that page and nothing here is a picture of the Librarian at all.
